syllabus.name: AQA GCSE Biology (8461), Paper 1, Higher tier

units.title: Cell structure and microscopy
points: Label the structures of animal, plant and bacterial cells and state their functions
Compare eukaryotic and prokaryotic cells and give examples of each
Explain how cell specialisation and differentiation suit a cell's function
Calculate magnification, image size and real size in µm and mm
Describe how to use a light microscope to observe and draw cells (RP1)
Compare light and electron microscopes in resolution and magnification
Explain order of magnitude and standard form for cell sizes
Describe how sperm, nerve and muscle cells are adapted

units.title: Cell division and stem cells
points: Describe the stages of the cell cycle including interphase and mitosis
Explain why mitosis produces genetically identical diploid cells
Describe how the cell cycle is used in growth and repair
State the sources of embryonic and adult stem cells, and plant meristems
Evaluate the uses and risks of stem cells in medicine and therapy
Calculate the number of cells after repeated mitotic division

units.title: Transport in cells
points: Explain diffusion in terms of particle concentration and temperature
Describe factors affecting the rate of diffusion and give examples
Explain osmosis in terms of water potential across a partially permeable membrane
Explain the effects of osmosis on animal and plant cells
Investigate osmosis using plant tissue masses (RP3)
Calculate percentage change in mass and identify the isotonic point
Describe active transport and give examples such as root hair cells and the gut
Compare diffusion, osmosis and active transport

units.title: Principles of organisation and enzymes
points: Describe the levels of organisation from cells to organ systems
Explain how digestive enzymes break down carbohydrates, proteins and lipids
State where amylase, protease and lipase are produced and act
Explain the effect of temperature on enzyme activity and denaturation
Explain the effect of pH on enzyme activity and the optimum pH
Use the lock-and-key model to explain enzyme specificity
Describe how to test foods for sugars, starch, protein and lipids (RP4)
Investigate the effect of pH on amylase activity (RP5)

units.title: The circulatory system
points: Label the heart: atria, ventricles, valves, aorta and vena cava
Describe the double circulatory system and its advantages
Explain how the heart rate is controlled by the pacemaker
Describe arteries, veins and capillaries and relate structure to function
Describe the composition of blood and the function of each component
Explain how stents, statins and artificial valves treat heart disease
Calculate cardiac output from heart rate and stroke volume

units.title: Health and disease
points: Define health and describe causes of ill health
Describe risk factors for non-communicable disease, e.g. cancer and CHD
Explain how lifestyle and genetic factors interact in disease
Describe how benign and malignant tumours form
Interpret data on disease risk factors and correlations

units.title: Plant organs and transport
points: Describe the tissues of a leaf and their functions
Explain how the root hair cell and xylem are adapted for water uptake
Describe transpiration and factors affecting its rate
Explain translocation in the phloem and the role of sieve tubes
Label the structures of a leaf, stem and root from a diagram

units.title: Communicable diseases
points: State that communicable diseases are spread by pathogens: bacteria, viruses, fungi, protists
Describe measles, HIV and tobacco mosaic virus symptoms and spread
Describe salmonella and gonorrhoea and how their spread is controlled
Describe rose black spot and malaria, including the vector
Explain how pathogens cause damage and how diseases are transmitted
Suggest ways to reduce the spread of disease

units.title: Human defence and vaccination
points: Describe the non-specific defences: skin, mucus, cilia, stomach acid
Explain the role of white blood cells in phagocytosis and antibody production
Explain how vaccination gives immunity and prevents epidemics
Describe the immune response to a first and second infection
Evaluate the use of vaccination and herd immunity, including risks

units.title: Drugs, antibiotics and drug development
points: Describe the discovery and development of new drugs from plants
Explain how antibiotics work and why resistance develops
Explain why antibiotics do not work on viruses and painkillers only treat symptoms
Describe the stages of clinical trials including placebo and double-blind
Evaluate benefits and risks of antibiotic use and drug testing

units.title: Monoclonal antibodies (Higher)
points: Describe how monoclonal antibodies are produced from a single cell
Explain how monoclonal antibodies are used in pregnancy tests
Describe their use in cancer treatment and diagnosis
Evaluate the advantages and problems of monoclonal antibody therapy

units.title: Plant disease and defences
points: Describe plant diseases and their detection methods
Identify common plant diseases from symptoms and data
Describe physical, chemical and mechanical plant defences
Explain plant defences and adaptations such as thorns and poisons

units.title: Photosynthesis and limiting factors
points: Write the word and balanced equation for photosynthesis
Explain how light, temperature and CO2 limit the rate of photosynthesis
Interpret graphs of rate against light intensity and other factors
Explain how glucose is used: respiration, starch, cellulose, amino acids
Investigate the effect of light intensity on pondweed (RP6)
Explain how photosynthesis was investigated historically
Use limiting factor graphs to predict rate changes

units.title: Aerobic and anaerobic respiration
points: Write the equation for aerobic respiration and state energy uses
Compare aerobic and anaerobic respiration in muscles and yeast
Explain the effects of exercise on the body and response to oxygen debt
Describe metabolism and the role of the liver in lactic acid breakdown
Interpret data on respiration and exercise response

critics: realism 100: Every day is within what you usually sustain.
exam_prep 50: fewer than two spaced retrieval sessions; no light review on Thu 24 Dec
front_loading 100: Deadline work finishes with room to spare.
interleaving 100: Practice is mixed across subjects.
fragmentation 100: Sessions are a workable length.
neglect 100: Every active goal has time.

points: Use arithmetic and geometric sequences, nth term and sum formulas
Use sigma notation and apply the binomial theorem
Find sums of finite arithmetic and geometric series
Solve financial problems: compound interest, depreciation, annuities
Use counting principles, permutations and combinations
Solve problems on the binomial expansion with rational indices

units.title: Number and algebra
points: Apply laws of exponents with rational exponents
Solve exponential equations using logarithms
Use the laws of logarithms, including change of base
Solve logarithmic and exponential inequalities
Sketch and analyse exponential and logarithmic graphs
Solve equations of the form a^x = b using logarithms

units.title: Proof and mathematical induction
points: Use direct proof and proof by contradiction
Use proof by counterexample
Prove statements by mathematical induction
Apply proof to divisibility and inequality statements
Distinguish when each method is appropriate
Construct rigorous arguments with clear reasoning

units.title: Permutations
points: Counting principles and permutations and combinations
Binomial coefficients and their relationship to combinations
Decompose rational expressions into partial fractions
Use partial fractions in integration and series work

units.title: Complex numbers
points: Perform arithmetic with complex numbers in Cartesian form
Find modulus, argument, conjugate and reciprocal
Use polar (trigonometric) and exponential forms
Multiply and divide complex numbers in polar form
Use De Moivre's theorem to find roots and powers
Solve polynomial equations with real coefficients, including conjugate roots
Represent complex numbers on an Argand diagram

units.title: Systems of linear equations
points: Solve 3x3 systems using row reduction / elimination
Identify unique, infinite and no-solution cases
Use matrices or technology to solve systems
Interpret geometric meaning of solutions for lines and planes
Apply partial fractions to rational expressions
Solve linear equations with polynomial identity methods

units.title: Functions and graphs
points: Find domain, range, inverse and composite functions
Use the factor and remainder theorems
Find sums and products of polynomial roots
Sketch rational functions with asymptotes and intercepts
Identify odd, even and self-inverse functions
Use the modulus function and solve inequalities
Transform graphs: translations, stretches, reflections
Solve equations graphically and with technology

units.title: Functions
points: Use the discriminant to determine the nature of roots
Complete the square and find vertex, axis of symmetry
Solve quadratic inequalities
Find the roots of polynomials, including multiplicity
Solve equations reducible to quadratic form

units.title: Triangle trigonometry
points: Use the sine and cosine rules and area formula
Solve problems using bearings and 3D figures
Use reciprocal trigonometric ratios (sec, cosec, cot)
Use Pythagorean and quotient identities
Solve trigonometric equations with compound angles
Apply inverse trigonometric functions and their domains

units.title: Circular functions and identities
points: Convert between degrees and radians and use arc length and sector area
Use the unit circle and reference angles
Apply compound and double angle identities
Use symmetry to simplify and solve trigonometric expressions
Sketch trigonometric functions and identify transformations
Solve trigonometric equations in given intervals

units.title: Further trigonometry
points: Define and use inverse trigonometric functions, including their domains and ranges
Solve equations using inverse trigonometric functions
Apply the double angle identity for tangent
Apply compound angle identities to solve equations

units.title: Vectors
points: Use vector notation, addition, subtraction and scalar multiplication
Find magnitude and unit vectors in 2D and 3D
Compute scalar (dot) product and cross product
Find angles between vectors
Solve equations of lines and planes
Find intersections and shortest distances involving lines and planes

units.title: Statistics and probability
points: Use descriptive statistics: mean, median, quartiles, standard deviation, IQR
Interpret box plots, histograms and cumulative frequency
Calculate probabilities using sample spaces, Venn diagrams and tree diagrams
Apply conditional probability and independent events
Use Bayes' theorem
Solve problems with mutually exclusive and exhaustive events

units.title: Probability distributions
points: Use discrete random variables and probability mass functions
Find expected value, variance and standard deviation
Work with the binomial distribution and its conditions
Use the normal distribution and standardisation
Find probabilities using normal distribution and inverse normal
Use probability density functions and expectation algebra

units.title: Limits and differential calculus
points: Understand informal limits and convergence
Differentiate from first principles
Differentiate polynomial, exponential, logarithmic and trigonometric functions
Apply product, quotient and chain rules
Differentiate inverse and reciprocal trigonometric functions
Use implicit differentiation
Apply L'Hopital's rule
Find tangent and normal equations

units.title: Applications of differential calculus
points: Analyse increasing/decreasing behaviour using first derivative
Find stationary points and classify them
Use the second derivative, concavity and points of inflection
Solve optimisation problems
Solve kinematics problems with displacement, velocity and acceleration

units.title: Integration
points: Find antiderivatives of standard functions
Compute definite and indefinite integrals
Use definite integrals for areas and volumes of revolution
Apply integration by substitution
Apply integration by parts
Apply partial fractions to integration

units.title: Calculus
points: Solve first-order differential equations by separation of variables
Use an integrating factor for linear first-order equations
Apply Euler's method to approximate solutions
Use Maclaurin series for standard functions
Use Taylor series and error bounds
Model real contexts with differential equations

units.title: Internal assessment: Mathematical exploration
points: Choose a topic with sufficient mathematical content for HL
Formulate a clear research question
Develop the mathematics coherently and rigorously
Justify methods and evaluate results
Include correct notation, graphs and diagrams
Reflect on limitations and possible extensions
Present a well-structured written report

critics: realism 100: Every day is within what you usually sustain.
exam_prep 50: fewer than two spaced retrieval sessions; no light review on Mon 3 May
front_loading 100: Deadline work finishes with room to spare.
interleaving 100: Practice is mixed across subjects.
fragmentation 100: Sessions are a workable length.
neglect 100: Every active goal has time.

quality.strategy: 24 topics revised and practised in order, 8 mixed reviews, 6 timed Physics sections, light final day.

units.title: Units and Measurements
points: Convert between SI units and use fundamental and derived units
Find dimensions of physical quantities and check dimensional consistency
Apply dimensional analysis to derive relations and convert units
Use significant figures and rounding correctly in results
Compute errors: absolute, relative, percentage, and in combined quantities
Use least count and vernier/screw gauge readings

units.title: Kinematics
points: Distinguish frame of reference, distance, displacement, speed and velocity
Interpret position-time and velocity-time graphs
Solve uniformly accelerated motion with the three equations of motion
Handle relative velocity in one and two dimensions
Analyse projectile motion: range, maximum height, time of flight
Solve uniform circular motion: angular speed, centripetal acceleration

units.title: Laws of Motion
points: Apply Newton's three laws and the concept of inertia and momentum
Use impulse-momentum theorem and conservation of linear momentum
Solve equilibrium of concurrent forces using free-body diagrams
Analyse static and kinetic friction, including rolling friction
Solve dynamics of uniform circular motion: level and banked roads
Handle connected bodies, pulleys and constraint relations

units.title: Work, Energy and Power
points: Compute work done by constant and variable forces
Apply the work-energy theorem to find speeds and displacements
Use potential energy of a spring and conservation of mechanical energy

quality.strategy: 22 topics revised and practised in order, 2 timed papers (SAA-C03 exam), light final day. Time is tight, so sessions are short.

units.title: IAM, Organizations and access control
points: Write IAM policies and use roles for cross-account access
Apply permission boundaries and service control policies
Use IAM Identity Center for workforce SSO with external IdPs
Organise accounts with AWS Organizations OUs and Control Tower
Choose managed policies over inline for reusable permissions
Troubleshoot access denied using policy evaluation logic

units.title: VPC network security and inspection
points: Configure security groups versus network ACLs correctly
Use VPC endpoints (gateway and interface) and AWS PrivateLink
Deploy AWS WAF managed and rate-based rules
Compare Shield Standard and Shield Advanced protection
Use Systems Manager Session Manager instead of a bastion host
Inspect traffic with VPC Flow Logs and Network Firewall

units.title: Threat detection
points: GuardDuty findings for anomalous and malicious activity
Macie for S3 PII detection and classification
Security Hub for aggregating findings across accounts
When each service is the right answer in a scenario

units.title: Encryption, KMS and secrets management
points: Design encryption at rest with KMS customer-managed keys
Use multi-region keys and key rotation for cross-region data
Encrypt S3 objects and EBS volumes with KMS and default keys
Terminate TLS with ACM certificates on ALB, NLB and CloudFront
Rotate database credentials with Secrets Manager versus Parameter Store
Detect sensitive data and threats with Macie, GuardDuty and Security Hub

units.title: Secrets management and bastion alternatives
points: Secrets Manager rotation patterns versus Parameter Store SecureString
When each secrets service is the right design choice
Bastion host versus Systems Manager Session Manager (Session Manager wins)

units.title: Multi-tier and loosely coupled compute
points: Design multi-tier architectures with public and private subnets
Place compute on EC2, containers (ECS, EKS) or Lambda appropriately
Scale fleets with Auto Scaling groups and target tracking
Serve traffic with ALB, NLB and Gateway Load Balancer
Decouple layers with SQS queues and SNS topics
Route events with EventBridge and apply microservice principles

units.title: High availability and multi-AZ design
points: Choose Multi-AZ over single-instance designs for availability
Use Route 53 failover, latency and geolocation routing with health checks
Compare RDS Multi-AZ with read replicas
Design stateless tiers that survive instance failure
Use Elastic Beanstalk environments for managed deployments
Plan bastion-free, highly available access patterns

units.title: Backup, DR and cross-region resilience
points: Distinguish backup-restore, pilot light, warm standby and active-active
Set RPO and RTO targets and pick the matching DR pattern
Replicate S3 with CRR/SRR and Replication Time Control
Use DynamoDB global tables, PITR and on-demand backups
Protect data with AWS Backup across services
Use Aurora Global Database for cross-region recovery

units.title: Queuing, messaging and decoupling
points: Tune SQS visibility timeout and retry policies
Configure dead-letter queues to capture failed messages
Choose SQS standard versus FIFO for ordering needs
Fan out with SNS to multiple subscribers
Orchestrate retries and compensation with Step Functions
Apply idempotency to make retried processing safe

units.title: Storage performance
points: Select EBS volume types (gp3, io2 Block Express, st1, sc1)
Tune EFS performance and throughput modes
Choose between FSx for Lustre, Windows and NetApp ONTAP
Size S3 throughput for high request rates
Match Instance Store versus EBS to workload needs
Configure RAID and multiple volumes for IOPS targets

units.title: Caching and content delivery
points: Design CloudFront distributions with cache behaviours and TTLs
Configure CloudFront origin failover and signed URLs
Choose Lambda@Edge versus CloudFront Functions
Use Global Accelerator for non-HTTP anycast traffic
Compare ElastiCache with DAX for database caching
Place caching layers to reduce latency and load

units.title: In-memory and DAX caching for databases
points: ElastiCache (Valkey/Redis OSS) for read-heavy and session data
DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) for microsecond DynamoDB reads
Trade-offs between ElastiCache, DAX and on-demand caching
Cache invalidation and TTL strategies

units.title: Database performance and scaling
points: Scale reads with RDS and Aurora read replicas (5 versus 15)
Use Aurora serverless and Global Database for variable or global load
Pick DynamoDB partition keys and indexes for performance
Use DynamoDB on-demand versus provisioned capacity
Optimise RDS instance classes and storage for workload
Apply read/write splitting in the application tier

units.title: Aurora DSQL and distributed database options
points: Aurora DSQL for distributed PostgreSQL at scale
Positioning against Aurora Global Database and DynamoDB global tables
When a distributed SQL database is the right design choice

units.title: Serverless and API performance
points: Configure Lambda provisioned and reserved concurrency
Use Lambda SnapStart to cut cold starts
Throttle and cache at API Gateway with usage plans
Create and manage REST and HTTP APIs
Choose synchronous versus asynchronous invocation patterns
Design responsive serverless event-driven workflows

units.title: EC2 and compute cost optimisation
points: Compare On-Demand, Savings Plans and Reserved Instances
Apply Spot instances to interruption-tolerant workloads
Choose Compute Savings Plans for Lambda and Fargate coverage
Right-size instances using Compute Optimizer
Match instance families to workload type
Use Auto Scaling schedules to cut idle capacity

units.title: Cost Optimization Hub and right-sizing tooling
points: Cost Optimization Hub for consolidated recommendations
Compute Optimizer for EC2, ASG, EBS and Lambda right-sizing
Acting on rightsizing and idle-resource findings

units.title: Storage cost optimisation
points: Select S3 storage classes including Intelligent-Tiering and Glacier tiers
Write S3 lifecycle rules to transition and expire objects
Use S3 Storage Lens for visibility and recommendations
Choose EBS types and snapshots economically
Move cold data to archival storage for databases and file systems
Deduplicate and compress backup data with AWS Backup

units.title: Networking and data transfer cost
points: Use VPC endpoints to avoid NAT Gateway data charges
Weigh S3 Transfer Acceleration against its cost
Serve outbound traffic through CloudFront
Place resources in the right region and AZ for cost
Understand cross-AZ and internet egress pricing
Choose single-NAT versus per-AZ NAT designs for cost

units.title: Cost governance and monitoring
points: Set AWS Budgets alerts and Cost Anomaly Detection
Use Cost Explorer and Cost and Usage Reports to analyse spend
Design pay-per-request versus provisioned serverless models
Apply tagging strategies for cost allocation
Use Savings Plans recommendations to cut recurring spend
Recognise managed services that remove operational cost

units.title: Generative AI cost levers (Bedrock)
points: Model selection to control per-token cost
Prompt Caching to reduce repeated input cost
Provisioned Throughput versus on-demand for steady workloads
Batch Inference for cost-efficient bulk jobs

units.title: Event-driven orchestration with Step Functions
points: Step Functions for orchestrating retries and compensating transactions
EventBridge buses for routing events between services
Choosing Step Functions versus SQS/SNS for workflow coordination
Decoupling producers and consumers in event-driven designs

fragmentation 81: 4 sessions are much shorter than ideal.
neglect 100: Every active goal has time.

units.title: Human Development
points: Describe normal growth, development milestones and screening in infancy and childhood
Outline pubertal changes and adolescent cognitive and psychosocial development
Identify normal age-related findings and care in adulthood and older adulthood
Apply routine preventive care, vaccinations and safety counselling by age group
Recognise normal variation such as constitutional delay of growth

units.title: Biostatistics & Epidemiology/Population Health
points: Interpret sensitivity, specificity, predictive values and likelihood ratios
Calculate and interpret relative risk, odds ratio, attributable risk and NNT
Recognise study designs and their biases, including selection and recall bias
Interpret confidence intervals, p-values and statistical power
Apply screening principles and measures of population health
Distinguish incidence from prevalence and crude from adjusted rates

units.title: Behavioral Health & Nervous Systems/Special
points: Classify psychotic, mood, anxiety and personality disorders by criteria
Identify neurotransmitters and drug mechanisms relevant to psychiatric illness
Localise lesions by pattern of motor, sensory and cranial nerve deficits
Recognise stroke syndromes, demyelinating disease and CNS tumours
Describe dementia, delirium and substance use disorders
Outline embryology and vascular anatomy of the brain and spinal cord
Recognise disorders of special senses: vision, hearing, balance, smell and taste

units.title: Blood & Lymphoreticular/Immune Systems
points: Interpret complete blood count, smear and iron studies in anaemia
Classify haemoglobinopathies, thalassaemias and haemolytic anaemias
Describe platelet disorders and coagulation pathways, including haemophilia and von Willebrand disease
Recognise leukaemias, lymphomas and myeloproliferative neoplasms
Outline transfusion reactions and blood product use
Identify infections and malignancies of lymphoid tissue and spleen
Describe anticoagulant and antiplatelet pharmacology

units.title: Blood & Lymphoreticular/Immune Systems
points: Distinguish humoral, cell-mediated, complement and phagocyte immunodeficiencies
Recognise HIV infection, AIDS complications and immune reconstitution syndrome
Classify hypersensitivity reactions types I to IV with examples
Describe transplant rejection and graft-versus-host disease
Explain immunomodulating drug mechanisms and adverse effects
Outline vaccine types, indications and adverse effects

units.title: Musculoskeletal, skin and subcutaneous tissue
points: Distinguish inflammatory arthritides and crystal arthropathies
Recognise bone disorders: osteoporosis, osteomalacia, Paget disease and fractures
Localise muscle and nerve lesions causing weakness
Classify primary skin lesions and describe common dermatitides
Identify skin infections, blistering diseases and cutaneous malignancies
Recognise soft tissue tumours and inherited connective tissue disorders
Describe antibiotics, steroids and immunosuppressants used in these conditions

units.title: Cardiovascular system
points: Relate cardiac embryology and congenital lesions to presentation
Interpret murmurs, jugular venous pulse and ECG findings
Describe ischaemic heart disease and myocardial infarction
Outline cardiomyopathies, valvular disease and pericardial disease
Recognise arrhythmias and conduction disorders by mechanism
Explain heart failure and shock pathophysiology and treatment
Describe lipid-lowering, antihypertensive and antiarrhythmic drugs
Identify vasculitides and vascular disease

units.title: Respiratory & Renal/Urinary Systems
points: Interpret pulmonary function tests and blood gases
Distinguish obstructive and restrictive lung diseases
Recognise pneumonia, tuberculosis and lung abscess
Describe pulmonary embolism, hypertension and adult respiratory distress syndrome
Identify lung carcinoma subtypes and paraneoplastic syndromes
Outline sleep apnoea and pleural diseases
Describe bronchodilators, corticosteroids and other respiratory drugs

units.title: Respiratory & Renal/Urinary Systems
points: Apply renal physiology: glomerular filtration, clearance and acid-base handling
Classify nephrotic and nephritic syndromes by histology and presentation
Recognise acute kidney injury, chronic kidney disease and electrolyte disorders
Describe urinary tract infections, stones and obstruction
Identify renal tumours and congenital urinary anomalies
Explain diuretics, acid-base therapies and nephrotoxic drugs

units.title: Gastrointestinal system
points: Localise gastrointestinal disease by symptoms and anatomy
Describe oesophageal and gastric disorders, including peptic ulcer disease and reflux
Recognise inflammatory bowel disease, malabsorption and coeliac disease
Outline liver disease: hepatitis, cirrhosis, portal hypertension and liver failure
Identify biliary and pancreatic disorders
Recognise gastrointestinal bleeding and tumours
Explain proton pump inhibitors, antiemetics and laxatives

units.title: Reproductive & Endocrine Systems
points: Outline gonadal embryology and sexual differentiation disorders
Describe menstrual cycle physiology and menstrual disorders
Recognise pregnancy complications, including ectopic pregnancy and pre-eclampsia
Identify infections and neoplasms of the female and male reproductive tracts
Describe contraception and infertility causes
Explain hormonal therapies and drugs affecting uterine tone

units.title: Reproductive & Endocrine Systems
points: Interpret thyroid, adrenal and pituitary function tests
Distinguish hyperthyroidism, hypothyroidism and thyroid nodules
Recognise diabetes mellitus, its complications and acute presentations
Describe adrenal disorders, including Cushing syndrome and Addison disease
Identify pituitary adenomas and their mass effects
Explain insulin, oral hypoglycaemics and hormone replacement
Recognise parathyroid and calcium metabolism disorders

units.title: Multisystem Processes & Disorders
points: Describe nutritional deficiencies, obesity and vitamin toxicities
Explain sepsis, systemic inflammatory response and shock
Recognise inherited metabolic and lysosomal storage diseases
Outline oncogenesis, tumour markers and paraneoplastic syndromes
Describe immune-mediated multisystem diseases and amyloidosis
Apply principles of pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics
Recognise adverse drug reactions and toxicology syndromes
Describe effects of ageing and environmental injury on multiple systems

units.title: Microbiology and infectious disease
points: Distinguish bacterial structure, virulence factors and culture characteristics
Describe viral replication and latency for major viral families
Recognise fungal and parasitic infections by presentation
Match organisms to classic clinical syndromes and laboratory findings
Identify notifiable infections and infection control principles
Explain antibiotic, antiviral and antifungal mechanisms and resistance

units.title: Pharmacology principles
points: Apply absorption, distribution, metabolism and elimination to dosing
Relate mechanism of action to receptor types and signal transduction
Predict dose-response, potency, efficacy and therapeutic index
Recognise drug interactions via CYP450 induction and inhibition
Identify antidotes and management of overdose
Describe autonomic drug effects by receptor subtype

units.title: Biochemistry and molecular biology
points: Describe glycolysis, gluconeogenesis, TCA cycle and oxidative phosphorylation
Identify enzyme deficiencies causing metabolic disease and their presentations
Outline lipid, amino acid and nucleotide metabolism disorders
Explain DNA replication, transcription, translation and mutations
Recognise chromosomal abnormalities and inheritance patterns
Describe cell cycle regulation, apoptosis and oncogenes
Relate vitamins and cofactors to deficiency syndromes

units.title: Cell biology and histology
points: Identify tissue types and organ histology on microscopy
Describe cell organelles and cytoskeletal elements and their defects
Explain cell membrane transport, including channels and pumps
Recognise cell injury, necrosis and apoptosis morphologically
Outline inflammation, repair and wound healing
Describe extracellular matrix and connective tissue components

units.title: Anatomy and embryology
points: Identify gross structures, foramina and relations in each body region
Relate nerve injuries to patterns of motor and sensory loss
Describe embryological development of each organ system
Recognise congenital anomalies from developmental failure
Interpret cross-sectional and imaging anatomy
Trace blood supply, drainage and lymphatic routes

units.title: Social Sciences
points: Apply patient-centred interviewing and shared decision-making
Describe informed consent and confidentiality obligations
Recognise health disparities and social determinants of health
Explain quality improvement, patient safety and medical error reporting
Outline health care systems, insurance and access
Identify ethical and legal principles in clinical scenarios

critics: realism 100: Every day is within what you usually sustain.
exam_prep 50: fewer than two spaced retrieval sessions; no light review on Fri 12 Mar
front_loading 100: Deadline work finishes with room to spare.
interleaving 100: Practice is mixed across subjects.
fragmentation 100: Sessions are a workable length.
neglect 100: Every active goal has time.

syllabus.name: Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind

units.title: The Cognitive Revolution
points: Trace how Homo sapiens came to dominate other human species
Explain the role of gossip and shared myths in large-group cooperation
Distinguish the Cognitive Revolution from later revolutions in the book's argument
Describe what archaeology and genetics say about early foragers

units.title: The Agricultural Revolution
points: Explain the book's argument that farming was 'history's biggest fraud'
Describe the costs of agriculture for health, diet and workload
Follow how surplus food supported elites, states and written records
Weigh the counterarguments to the book's luxury-trap thesis

units.title: The Unification of Humankind
points: Explain money as a system of shared trust
Trace how empires spread common cultures and norms
Describe religion's role in unifying large populations
Show how commerce, empire and religion wove separate worlds together

units.title: The Scientific Revolution
points: Explain the discovery of ignorance as a driver of modern science
Link science, European imperialism and capitalism
Describe how credit and trust in the future fuelled growth
Assess the book's claim that progress and happiness are not the same

units.title: The End of Homo Sapiens
points: Summarise the book's speculations on genetic engineering and cyborgs
Discuss the open questions it raises about the future of our species
Compare these projections with the book's own earlier arguments

stages: Planning Learn guitar from zero: open chords to playing my first full
Fitting 41 pieces of work into your free time
quality.strategy: 8 stages, each with a lesson, practice and a milestone check.

syllabus.name: Guitar from zero to a first full song

units.title: Holding the guitar and first notes
points: Sit or stand with the guitar balanced and the neck at a comfortable angle
Tune all six strings with a tuner, then by matching fretted notes
Number strings and frets and find any note by name
Pluck single notes cleanly with a pick and with fingers
Press strings just behind the fret without muting neighbours

units.title: Strumming and rhythm basics
points: Keep a steady down-strum at a slow tempo with a metronome
Strum from the wrist and elbow without tensing the shoulder
Count quarter and eighth notes out loud while strumming
Play down-up eighths evenly, brushing all strings
Mute unwanted strings to stop ringing between strums

units.title: First open chords: Em, Am, E, A
points: Fret Em with two fingers and check every string rings
Play Am and A with clean, arched fingers
Play E major and hear its difference from Em
Change between Em and Am without stopping the strum
Use a chord pressure check: play each string one at a time

units.title: Open chords: C, G, D, Dm
points: Play open C with the ring finger on the third fret of the A string
Play G with fingers placed to allow fast changes to C and D
Play D and Dm with the thin strings ringing clearly
Swap between C, G and D in slow, even changes
Anchor common fingers between chord pairs to reduce movement

units.title: Changing chords in time
points: Change chords on the count without breaking the strum
Use one-minute changes to measure how many swaps you can make
Keep the strumming hand moving while the fretting hand moves
Simplify to down-strums on the beat, then add ups
Recover smoothly from a muffled or missed chord

units.title: Common strumming patterns
points: Play the down-down-up-up-down-up eighth-note pattern
Play a pattern with a missed down-strum for a reggae feel
Accent the backbeat and keep the arm swinging
Count in 4/4 and feel bars and phrases
Loop a four-chord pattern without losing the beat

units.title: Barre-free extras: capo, F alternatives
points: Use a capo to move easy chord shapes to a new key
Play Fmaj7 and F with a small barre as an alternative
Play a simple walk-up with bass notes between chords
Add a hammer-on and pull-off within a chord shape
Choose a key that fits your voice using the capo

units.title: Playing your first full song
points: Read a chord chart with bars and repeat signs
Break the song into verse and chorus and learn each section
Play the whole song at a slow tempo with the metronome
Bring it up to full tempo with no stops
Play it through with the original recording
Keep going after mistakes and finish the song

syllabus.name: Acids, Bases and pH — class quiz

units.title: Properties and definitions of acids and bases
points: List the characteristic properties of acids and bases, including taste, feel and litmus colour
Write the Arrhenius/Brønsted–Lowry definition of an acid and of a base
Identify the conjugate acid–base pairs in a given reaction
Classify species as Lewis acids or Lewis bases by electron-pair acceptance or donation
Explain how acid–base theories became broader from Arrhenius to Brønsted–Lowry to Lewis

units.title: Strong and weak acids and bases
points: Distinguish strong from weak acids and bases using the degree of ionisation
Write equations showing full ionisation of strong acids and partial ionisation of weak acids
Explain how dilution and concentration affect pH for strong versus weak acids
Calculate percent ionisation from Ka or from concentrations
Use Ka, Kb and Kw to compare acid and base strength

units.title: Water, Kw and pH calculations
points: Calculate pH from [H+] as -log[H+] and pOH from [OH-]
Convert between pH, pOH, [H+] and [OH-] using pH + pOH = 14
Work out [OH-] from a given pH or [H+] in an aqueous solution
Use the pH scale to classify a solution as acidic, neutral or basic
Use the heat of dissociation of water to explain why pH 7 is neutral only at 25 °C

units.title: Determination of pH with probeware
points: Use a pH probe or pH meter to measure the pH of a range of solutions
Calibrate the probe with buffer solutions of known pH before measuring
Compare probeware readings with indicator or calculated pH values and discuss precision
Investigate how pH changes on dilution or on adding acid or base

units.title: Neutralisation, salts and titration
points: Write balanced equations for acid plus base and acid plus carbonate reactions
Name the salt formed by a given acid–base reaction
Perform a titration to find the concentration of an unknown acid or base
Carry out titration calculations using moles and the reaction ratio
Predict whether a salt solution is acidic, basic or neutral from its parent acid and base

units.title: Buffers and pH regulation
points: Describe how a buffer resists pH change on adding small amounts of acid or base
Write the equations showing a buffer reacting with added H+ and OH-
Identify a buffer system from its components, e.g. a weak acid with its salt

Compute binomial probabilities using C(n,r) p^r (1−p)^(n−r)
Find mean and variance of a binomial: np and np(1−p)
Use a given probability distribution table and its expectation
sessions.how: Work through each key point with one example, then do three questions without notes and check them.

sessions.title: Recall check: 6 topics
sessions.aim: Pull Sample spaces and events to Binomial and discrete distributions back from memory after a gap.
points: Sample spaces and events: List outcomes of experiments and count equally likely ones
Sample spaces and events: Use Venn diagrams and set notation for unions, intersections, complements
Counting methods for probability: Use the multiplication principle for successive choices
Counting methods for probability: Count arrangements with permutations and selections with combinations
Independent events and tree diagrams: Apply P(A∩B) = P(A)P(B) for independent events
Independent events and tree diagrams: Test whether events are independent from given probabilities
Conditional probability: Write conditional probability in notation P(A|B) and interpret B as the new sample space
Conditional probability: Apply P(A|B) = P(A∩B)/P(B) using counts and probabilities
Law of total probability and Bayes' theorem: Split an event by a partition and sum conditional cases
sessions.how: Without notes, write what you remember and do one question on each. Check, then fix only the gaps.

identity.subject: Philosophie

units.title: La conscience, l'inconscient, le sujet
points: Distinguer conscience immédiate, conscience réfléchie et conscience de soi
Exposer la découverte freudienne de l'inconscient et ses topiques
Problématiser l'unité du sujet entre conscience et inconscient
Analyser un texte de Descartes, Locke, Nietzsche ou Freud sur le sujet

units.title: La perception et autrui
points: Distinguer sensation, perception et interprétation du donné
Comparer les analyses de la perception chez Descartes, Berkeley et Merleau-Ponty
Montrer comment autrui est un autre moi et une altérité irréductible
Expliquer le rôle du regard d'autrui (Hegel, Sartre) dans la constitution du soi

units.title: Le langage
points: Distinguer signe, symbole, langage animal et langage humain
Expliquer le caractère conventionnel et arbitraire des signes
Analyser les fonctions du langage : nommer, signifier, communiquer, agir
Discuter l'idée que les limites de mon langage sont les limites de mon monde

units.title: La raison et le réel : la vérité et la croyance
points: Distinguer opinion, croyance, doute et savoir
Exposer la méthode cartésienne du doute et le cogito
Expliquer la démarche expérimentale et le rôle de l'hypothèse
Discuter les critères de la vérité : cohérence, correspondance, évidence

units.title: La science et l'expérience
points: Distinguer science et technique, théorie et observation
Expliquer le rôle de l'induction et sa critique par Hume
Analyser les révolutions scientifiques et la notion de paradigme (Kuhn, Bachelard)
Discuter les limites de la connaissance scientifique et la notion de réfutabilité

units.title: La liberté et le déterminisme
points: Distinguer libre arbitre, liberté d'action et liberté politique
Exposer le déterminisme et les objections qu'il oppose à la liberté
Analyser le rapport entre liberté et nécessité (Spinoza, Leibniz)
Discuter l'idée d'une liberté construite par la connaissance de soi

units.title: L'art et le beau
points: Distinguer le beau, l'agréable et le sublime (Kant)
Analyser le rapport entre art, imitation et création
Expliquer la fonction de l'art : expression, connaissance, dévoilement
Discuter la question du jugement de goût et de l'universalité du beau

units.title: La nature
points: Distinguer nature et culture, nature et artifice
Analyser la nature comme norme ou comme modèle (droit naturel, retour à la nature)
Discuter la maîtrise technique de la nature et ses limites
Expliquer le rapport entre nature et liberté humaine

units.title: Le vivant
points: Distinguer le vivant de la matière inerte et de la machine
Analyser la notion de finalité dans le vivant (Aristote, Kant)
Discuter les frontières du vivant : espèce, individu, ADN, biotechnologies
Problématiser les rapports entre l'homme et l'animal

units.title: Le travail et la technique
points: Distinguer travail, emploi, activité et loisir
Analyser la valeur du travail : peine, émancipation, aliénation (Hegel, Marx)
Expliquer le rôle de l'outil et de la machine dans la technique
Discuter les enjeux de la technique : maîtrise, dépendance, responsabilité

units.title: Le devoir et le bonheur
points: Distinguer le devoir moral et le désir de bonheur
Exposer les morales du devoir (Kant) et les morales du bonheur (eudémonisme, utilitarisme)
Problématiser le conflit entre obligation et inclination
Analyser la notion de bonheur et son caractère relatif

units.title: La morale, le droit et la politique ; l'État et
points: Distinguer obligation morale, contrainte juridique et légitimité
Exposer la théorie du contrat social (Hobbes, Locke, Rousseau)
Analyser les formes de l'État : État de droit, État-providence, souveraineté
Discuter le rapport entre liberté individuelle et autorité politique

units.title: Le temps, l'existence et la mort
points: Distinguer temps vécu, temps mesuré et temps physique
Analyser la conscience du temps (Augustin, Bergson, Heidegger)
Discuter la question du sens de l'existence
Analyser le rapport de l'homme à sa mort (Épicure, Montaigne)

units.title: La religion
points: Distinguer foi, croyance religieuse et savoir rationnel
Analyser les fonctions de la religion : sens, cohésion, loi morale
Exposer les critiques de la religion (Feuerbach, Marx, Nietzsche, Freud)
Discuter le rapport entre religion et raison, religion et liberté de conscience

units.title: La logique et les mathématiques
points: Distinguer démontrer, prouver, argumenter et convaincre
Identifier les formes valides d'inférence et les sophismes
Expliquer la différence entre vérité et validité logique
Analyser la démonstration mathématique et son rapport à l'expérience

units.title: La philosophie et la métaphysique
points: Définir la philosophie et son rapport aux sciences et aux arts
Expliquer la démarche de la question philosophique et du problème
Analyser les questions métaphysiques : unité, être, cause, absolu
Situer quelques grandes démarches (Platon, Descartes, Kant, Hegel)

front_loading 100: Deadline work finishes with room to spare.
interleaving 100: Practice is mixed across subjects.
fragmentation 100: Sessions are a workable length.
neglect 100: Every active goal has time.

identity.edition: National Curriculum 2022-23 (HSSC-II), FBISE Annual Examination 2026 and onwards
identity.subject: Physics

units.title: Electrostatics
points: State Coulomb's law and apply it to systems of point charges
Define electric field and calculate field due to point charges and dipoles
Define electric flux and state Gauss's law with its applications
Derive field of a charged sphere, sheet and cylinder using Gauss's law
Define electric potential and relate potential gradient to field strength
Calculate electric potential energy of point charge systems
Define electron volt and convert between eV and joules
Describe capacitors, electric polarization and energy stored; charging and discharging

units.title: Current Electricity
points: Define current, drift velocity and current density; derive I = nAve
State and apply Ohm's law; describe resistance and resistivity of conductors
Describe effect of temperature on resistance of metals and semiconductors
Derive and use the formula for combination of resistors in series and parallel
State Kirchhoff's first and second laws and apply them to circuits
Solve circuit problems using Kirchhoff's laws
Calculate electrical power and energy dissipated in circuits
Describe the potentiometer and its use in measuring emf and potential difference

units.title: Electromagnetism
points: Define magnetic flux density and describe magnetic field due to a straight conductor
Describe the magnetic field of a solenoid and of a current loop
Calculate force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field
Calculate force on a moving charge and describe circular motion in a magnetic field
Determine torque on a current loop and describe the moving-coil galvanometer
Describe the construction and working of an ammeter and a voltmeter
Explain the working principle of a cathode ray oscilloscope

units.title: Electromagnetic Induction
points: State Faraday's law and Lenz's law and apply them to find induced emf
Relate induced emf to rate of change of flux and to motional emf
Define self-inductance and mutual inductance with their units
Calculate energy stored in an inductor
Describe the principle and working of an AC generator
Describe the principle and working of a transformer and energy losses
Explain eddy currents and their uses and drawbacks

units.title: Alternating Current
points: Define alternating current and describe its waveform, peak and rms values
Calculate reactance of a capacitor and an inductor
Determine impedance of series RLC circuits and draw phasor diagrams
Explain resonance in an AC circuit and use the resonant frequency formula
Describe power in AC circuits and the power factor
Describe the components and working of an AC generator and of a transformer in AC transmission
Explain advantages of AC over DC for transmission of electric power

units.title: Physics of Solids
points: Describe crystalline and amorphous solids and their properties
Describe energy bands in solids and classify conductors, insulators and semiconductors
Distinguish intrinsic and extrinsic semiconductors; describe p-type and n-type doping
Describe the p-n junction and its depletion region
Describe forward and reverse biasing of a diode and draw its characteristic curve
Describe the use of a diode as a rectifier
Describe the structure and working of an LED and a photodiode
Describe the structure of an npn transistor and the action of a transistor amplifier

units.title: Electronics
points: Explain logic gates AND, OR, NOT with truth tables
Explain universal gates NAND and NOR with truth tables
Combine gates to form simple logic circuits
Describe operational amplifier as an ideal amplifier and its use
Distinguish analogue and digital signals and describe digital electronics
Describe the working of a cathode ray oscilloscope in displaying signals

units.title: Dawn of Modern Physics
points: Describe the frame of reference and state Einstein's postulates of special relativity
Explain time dilation, length contraction and mass variation
Calculate mass-energy equivalence using E = mc²
Describe black body radiation and Planck's quantum hypothesis
Explain the photoelectric effect and state its laws
Use Einstein's photoelectric equation and describe the effect of intensity and frequency
Describe the Compton effect and its significance
Explain wave-particle duality and the de Broglie wavelength

units.title: Atomic Spectra
points: Describe the Bohr model of the hydrogen atom and its postulates
Derive and use the expression for energy levels and radii of hydrogen
Explain the origin of line spectra: emission and absorption spectra
Describe the spectral series of hydrogen and the Rydberg formula
Relate spectral lines to energy level transitions
Describe the limitations of the Bohr model and the idea of the laser
Describe the working of a laser and its applications

units.title: Nuclear Physics
points: Describe the structure of the nucleus, atomic number and mass number
Describe isotopes and the basic forces of nature
Define mass defect and calculate binding energy per nucleon
Describe radioactivity and the properties of alpha, beta and gamma radiation
State and use the radioactive decay law and half-life
Distinguish nuclear fission and nuclear fusion with examples
Describe nuclear reactors and the hazards and uses of nuclear radiation
Describe the uses of radioisotopes in medicine and industry

critics: realism 100: Every day is within what you usually sustain.
exam_prep 50: fewer than two spaced retrieval sessions; no light review on Tue 26 Jan
front_loading 100: Deadline work finishes with room to spare.
interleaving 100: Practice is mixed across subjects.
fragmentation 100: Sessions are a workable length.
neglect 100: Every active goal has time.

units.title: Ethical and Professional Standards
points: Apply the CFA Institute Code of Ethics and Standards of Professional Conduct to scenarios
Distinguish ethical duties to clients, employers and the investing public
Apply standards on integrity of capital markets and investment recommendations
Identify and manage conflicts of interest and disclosure requirements
Apply standards on performance presentation and GIPS fundamentals
Judge the appropriate conduct in practice-problem 'best action' cases

units.title: Quantitative Methods: Time Value of Money
points: Compute present and future values for lump sums and annuities
Solve for interest rate, number of periods and payment amounts
Distinguish nominal, effective and stated annual rates
Use cash flow worksheets on the approved calculator

units.title: Quantitative Methods: Statistics and Probability
points: Compute and interpret mean, median, variance and covariance
Apply probability rules, expected value and conditional probability
Describe normal, lognormal and binomial distributions
Apply sampling, central limit theorem and estimator properties
Conduct hypothesis tests and interpret p-values and test statistics
Interpret correlation, simple and multiple regression
Describe big data, machine learning and algorithmic trading basics

units.title: Economics: Microeconomics
points: Analyse demand and supply shifts and market equilibrium
Compute and interpret price, income and cross elasticities
Compare market structures: perfect competition, monopoly, monopolistic competition, oligopoly
Explain consumer theory and indifference curves
Relate production, costs and profit maximisation

units.title: Economics
points: Interpret national income accounting and GDP measures
Describe business cycle phases and economic indicators
Explain monetary and fiscal policy tools and their effects
Analyse inflation, unemployment and aggregate demand/supply
Explain exchange rate regimes and currency exchange determination
Describe international trade theories and trade restrictions
Summarise geopolitical and capital flow considerations for economies

units.title: Financial Statement Analysis
points: Describe the roles and elements of the income statement, balance sheet and cash flow statement
Interpret financial reporting standards and the IFRS/US GAAP framework
Trace how transactions flow through the core financial statements
Apply general accounting principles such as accrual and revenue recognition

units.title: Corporate Issuers
points: Evaluate capital budgeting projects using NPV, IRR and payback
Compute and interpret weighted average cost of capital
Describe capital structure theories and leverage effects
Explain corporate governance, ownership structures and stakeholder relations
Analyse business models, working capital management and short-term liquidity
Describe capital raising for public and private companies

units.title: Portfolio Management
points: Explain the portfolio approach and investor characteristics
Compute portfolio expected return and risk
Interpret diversification, covariance and correlation
Describe risk aversion, mean-variance optimisation and efficient frontier
Explain risk management, portfolio planning and the investment policy statement

units.title: Equity Investments
points: Describe market organisation, structure and trading mechanics
Compare order types, execution and market regulation basics
Explain market efficiency and its implications
Compare security market indices and their construction
Apply equity valuation concepts of intrinsic value, price multiples and present value models
Describe company analysis and industry analysis fundamentals

units.title: Fixed Income
points: Describe fixed income instruments and issuers
Explain features of coupon bonds, floating rate and money market instruments
Compute bond prices, yields and yield measures
Explain yield curve shapes and term structure theories
Analyse interest rate risk, duration and convexity
Describe securitisation and fixed income asset classes

units.title: Derivatives
points: Describe forwards, futures, options and swaps and their payoff profiles
Interpret futures pricing and forward pricing basics
Apply option pricing basics: intrinsic value, put-call parity, binomial and Black-Scholes intuition
Explain uses of derivatives: hedging, arbitrage and speculation

units.title: Alternative Investments
points: Describe hedge funds, private equity, real estate, commodities and infrastructure
Explain fee structures and incentive alignment in alternative investments
Describe diversification, liquidity and valuation issues of alternatives

critics: realism 100: Every day is within what you usually sustain.
exam_prep 50: fewer than two spaced retrieval sessions; no light review on Sun 11 Apr
front_loading 100: Deadline work finishes with room to spare.
interleaving 100: Practice is mixed across subjects.
fragmentation 100: Sessions are a workable length.
neglect 100: Every active goal has time.

quality.strategy: 9 parts at a steady pace, with written recaps.

units.title: Introduction
points: Outline Kahneman's two-system picture of the mind
Locate where each part of the book argues its case

units.title: Part 1: Two Systems
points: Distinguish System 1's fast automatic processing from System 2's effortful control
Explain cognitive ease, priming and the ideomotor effect
Show why System 2 is lazy and endorses System 1's suggestions
Recognise what attention can and cannot do at once

units.title: Part 2: Heuristics and Biases
points: Apply the law of small numbers to research and everyday claims
Explain anchoring and the anchoring index
Describe the availability heuristic and affect heuristic
Recognise representativeness, base-rate neglect and conjunction fallacy
Identify less-is-more and causal-base confusions

units.title: Part 3: Overconfidence
points: Explain the illusions of validity and skill in prediction
Describe formula vs. intuition in judging people
Give the conditions for intuitive expertise and why some professions fail them
Explain the outside view and how to take it
Critique cases where overconfidence is misplaced

units.title: Part 4: Choices
points: Apply prospect theory to gains, losses and risk
Explain loss aversion, reference points and the endowment effect
Describe framing effects and mental accounting
Explain fairness, regret and the disposition effect

units.title: Part 5: Two Selves
points: Explain duration neglect and the peak-end rule
Distinguish the experiencing self from the remembering self
Apply this to evaluations of well-being and policy

units.title: Conclusions
points: Summarise the two-system thesis and its limits
Critique the rationality model of economics in light of the evidence

units.title: Appendix A: Judgment under Uncertainty
points: Follow the original heuristics-and-biases argument
Relate it to the earlier development of the ideas

units.title: Appendix B: Choices, Values, and Frames
points: Follow the original prospect theory formulation
Connect it to the value function and framing effects

syllabus.name: Python with pandas for data analysis

units.title: Set up Python and run a script
points: Install Python and an editor such as VS Code or Jupyter
Create and activate a virtual environment
Install pandas and matplotlib with pip
Run a .py file and a notebook cell successfully
Read error messages and find the failing line

units.title: Python basics for data work
points: Assign variables and use the main types: int, float, str, bool
Write lists and dictionaries, index and slice them
Use if/elif/else and for loops over a list
Define a function with parameters and a return value
Use f-strings to build readable output
Translate a familiar Excel formula into Python code

units.title: Load and inspect a CSV
points: Import pandas with the standard import pandas as pd
Read a CSV with pd.read_csv, setting sep and encoding when needed
Inspect with head, tail, shape, columns and dtypes
Use info() and describe() to summarise a dataset
Spot wrong types such as numbers read as text

units.title: Select and filter rows and columns
points: Select columns with brackets and rows with loc and iloc
Filter with boolean conditions and combine them using & and |
Use isin and between for range and list checks
Sort with sort_values and take the top rows
Compare this to Excel's filter and VLOOKUP habits

units.title: Clean and reshape the data
points: Handle missing values with isna, dropna and fillna
Convert types with astype and to_datetime; parse dates
Rename columns and drop duplicates
Standardise messy text with str.strip, str.lower and str.replace
Use assign and the apply method to create derived columns
Detect outliers with describe or the IQR rule

units.title: Group, combine and summarise
points: Aggregate with groupby and agg (sum, mean, count)
Build pivot tables with pivot_table as in Excel
Merge and join two tables on a key column
Concatenate tables stacked with pd.concat
Chain steps with method chaining for readable code

units.title: Chart the results
points: Plot a line chart of a series over time
Draw a bar chart of category totals
Make a histogram and scatter plot
Label axes, titles and legends clearly
Save the figure as a PNG at good resolution

units.title: Work on your own real CSV end to end
points: Choose a dataset and state the question you want answered
Write a script that loads, cleans and summarises it
Produce two charts that answer your question
Export the cleaned table to a new CSV
Explain the findings in a short written summary
